title: Deterministically parse compact quota magnitudes without publishing false numbers
objective: Make the generic publication revalidator interpret only unambiguous directly-adjacent uppercase decimal SI count suffixes K, M, and B, while unsupported compact numeric forms fail the deterministic publication gate instead of persisting their leading digits as false quota amounts.
acceptance_criteria: A1: parse_quantity maps directly-adjacent uppercase K, M, and B to exact Decimal multipliers 1000, 1000000, and 1000000000, including 2.5K, slash resets, trailing units, and qualifier prefixes.
A2: the recognized magnitude suffix is consumed as part of the numeric token and never persisted as a unit; remaining reset and unit text retain current semantics.

A3: lowercase suffixes, separated single-letter magnitude forms, adjacent binary-looking forms, unknown suffixes, multiple suffixes, signs, and scientific notation produce amount=None; revalidate_quotas records numeric-looking fields as unparsed and deterministic=False.

A4: existing behavior remains exact for 100,000/day, 128 MB, 50%, decimal fractions, 1 build at a time, and metric _per_month fallback; parsing remains search-based for supported qualifier prefixes and raw strings remain unchanged.
A5: a live PostgreSQL publication persists 10K, 2K, and 1M as exact Quota amounts 10000, 2000, and 1000000, with matching immutable material facts and content hash.

A6: a live PostgreSQL publication attempt containing an unsupported compact magnitude creates no Offer, OfferVersion, or Quota and never persists a truncated leading amount; it follows the existing review/withhold gate semantics.
A7: documentation states the supported suffix boundary and fail-closed behavior without claiming structured qualifier semantics the schema does not represent.
A8: no provider-specific code, dependency, migration, fixture, configuration, feature-ledger, classifier, or model change is introduced.

A9: any Unicode punctuation or symbol directly adjacent before the numeric token fails closed, including U+FE62, U+FE63, U+2795, and U+2796, while whitespace-separated qualifier prefixes remain supported.

A10: compact multi-letter ordinary units such as ms, GB, Mbps, Kbps, and kB parse as units, while ambiguous KB/MB, IEC-looking KiB/MiB/GiB, single-letter unknowns, and repeated magnitude letters fail closed.
A11: text containing more than one numeric token fails closed, including versions, dates, malformed dotted sequences, and ranges; one-token qualifier text remains supported.

A12: a semantic Unicode sign token immediately before arbitrary Unicode whitespace and the sole number fails closed, while generic separated qualifier punctuation such as colon, parenthesis, and tilde remains supported.
A13: the entire trailing prefix token is scanned across Unicode separators, Cf controls, and non-sign punctuation; semantic plus, minus, hyphen, dash, and Pd forms fail closed before any number.

A14: when K, M, or B was consumed before an alphabetic continuation, only explicit rate-unit tokens Kbps, Mbps, and MBps are accepted as compact units; arbitrary Kfoo/Mfoo/Brequests forms fail closed.

fresh-context Level 2 evaluator: inspect parser boundaries, publication gate behavior, exact database rows, immutable material facts/content hash, regressions, and mutations
mutation_plan: M1 predicted RED: remove the magnitude multiplier application; K/M/B unit and live persistence tests must fail.
M2 predicted RED: relax the post-suffix token boundary so an adjacent binary-looking or multiple-suffix form is accepted; ambiguity tests must fail.
M3 predicted RED: remove the Unicode category guard; sign and punctuation adversarial cases must fail.
M4 predicted RED: reject every adjacent alphabetic token; compact ordinary-unit tests must fail.
M5 predicted RED: accept the first numeric match when multiple exist; version/date/range tests must fail.
M6 predicted RED: accept every multi-letter adjacent token as a unit; ambiguous KB/MB, IEC, and repeated-magnitude tests must fail.
M7 predicted RED: remove the trailing semantic sign-token guard; whitespace-separated sign tests must fail.
M8 predicted RED: inspect only ASCII-space separation or skip NFKC/name semantics; Unicode whitespace and normalized-sign tests must fail.
M9 predicted RED: stop the prefix scanner after one code point or stop skipping Cf controls; hidden-sign tests must fail.
M10 predicted RED: remove Pd/dash-name semantics; Unicode dash tests must fail.
M11 predicted RED: accept arbitrary alphabetic continuations after consumed K/M/B; Kfoo/Mfoo/Brequests tests must fail.
data_implications: No schema or migration change. Corrected exact Decimal values change future Quota rows, OfferVersion material_facts, and content_hash for compact SI quota evidence. Existing immutable rows are not rewritten.
security_privacy: No network, secret, authentication, authorization, or user-controlled URL change.
portability: Pure standard-library parsing and Decimal arithmetic; no platform-specific behavior.
z0_risk: High. False quota amounts can misstate capacity and recommendation fit. Unsupported forms must block automatic publication rather than guess.
